threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: Newbies always wait for the green man at Crossroads. The locals just bolt across, dodging bikes and cars like it's an Olympic sport.
Last night on the 59, a lad argued with the driver about his expired Oyster. Never seen someone so determined to ride for free!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a toddler selling homemade lemonade on the corner, while their mom bargained with a vintage dealer next door. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Prenzlauer Berg can you find a café that brews its coffee with water from the Spree. It’s like sipping a river's history.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they avoid the BART during a delay, opting for a bike instead. Tourists don't know the hidden gems in the alleys.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Last night at Civic Center, a guy in a sequined suit did a dance off with a saxophonist while we waited for the 21. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think every street festival means partying all night. In Gràcia, some locals just want to enjoy the quieter moments over coffee and a book.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they still use an umbrella at the slightest hint of rain, oblivious to the locals' dance with the downpour.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the tube' instead of 'the underground'—give it a few months, and you'll be seamlessly blending in with the locals.
Last night on the 133, a guy serenaded us with a ukulele. Everyone pretended to ignore him, but we all ended up humming along.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I found a late-night bakery with the best kaiserschmarrn, and the owner remembers my name after just two visits.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find late-night Späti DJs spinning records while you grab a beer. The blending of convenience and nightlife is unique to this city.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they instinctively avoid the Civic Center BART at night. That station's a mess; loud bangs and smoke aren't just for tourists.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo on the 31 Balboa, talking politics with a street performer. Only in San Francisco do you dress for the occasion while commuting.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think locals only drink vermut on weekends; you’ll see us sipping it through the week at the corner bars while discussing the latest train delays.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still look puzzled at the metro map, especially when the train suddenly stops and the announcements are in rapid-fire Catalan.
